Las etapas de descenso de los módulos lu: The descent stages of the Lunar Modules (like Apollo 11's Eagle) were left behind as launch pads.
Tres \"autos lunares\" eléctricos conduc: Three electric "moon buggies" driven by astronauts. Parked permanently on the Moon.
Paquetes de experimentos de superficie d: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Packages (seismometers, retroreflectors, etc.) left to do science after astronauts departed.
Sondas robóticas enviadas en los años 60: Robotic probes sent in the 1960s to prove soft landings were possible.
El primer rover en Marte (1997), llevado: The first rover on Mars (1997), delivered by the Pathfinder lander. Now permanently parked.
Rovers gemelos que funcionaron durante a: Twin rovers that operated for years. Both are now inactive monuments to Mars exploration.
Los primeros módulos de EE. UU. que func: The first U.S. landers to successfully operate on Mars (1976), remaining exactly where they touched down.
Phoenix excavó en busca de hielo de agua: Phoenix dug for water ice; InSight listened for marsquakes. Both eventually lost power.
El primer aparato que voló en otro plane: The first aircraft on another planet. Sustained rotor damage and became a stationary artifact.
Las primeras sondas de espacio profundo: Early deep-space probes that explored the outer planets. Now drifting silently out of the solar system.
Cartografió Vesta y Ceres. Se quedó sin: Mapped Vesta and Ceres. Ran out of fuel and remains in a perpetual, unpowered orbit around Ceres.
La primera nave en orbitar un asteroide: First spacecraft to orbit and land on an asteroid. Left resting on the surface of 433 Eros.
Revolucionario telescopio cazador de exo: Revolutionary exoplanet-hunting telescope that ran out of fuel and is drifting in an Earth-trailing orbit.

Neil Armstrong y Buzz Aldrin (Michael Co: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin (Michael Collins, in orbit)
Unos 7 m de alto con las patas desplegad: About 7 m tall with its legs deployed
El módulo lunar fue la primera nave trip: The Lunar Module was the first crewed spacecraft built to fly only in the vacuum of space. It had two parts: the descent stage, with the braking engine and four legs, and the ascent stage, the astronauts' small cabin.
Para volver, la etapa de ascenso despegó: To return, the ascent stage lifted off using the descent stage as its launch pad. That base stayed on the Moon with a plaque on one of its legs that reads: "Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon."
Seis etapas de descenso se quedaron en l: Six descent stages remain on the Moon: those of Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16 and 17.
Sigue en la Base Tranquilidad, rodeada d: It is still at Tranquility Base, surrounded by footprints, the flag and the experiments Apollo 11 left behind.
Vehículo eléctrico de cuatro ruedas para: Four-wheeled electric vehicle for two astronauts
Unos 210 kg; podía cargar unos 490 kg: About 210 kg; it could carry about 490 kg
Dos baterías de plata y zinc, no recarga: Two non-rechargeable silver-zinc batteries; one motor in each wheel
El LRV viajaba plegado en un costado del: The LRV travelled folded up on the side of the Lunar Module and unfolded on the surface. Thanks to it, astronauts could travel several kilometres from the module and carry more tools and samples.
Llevaba una antena para hablar directame: It carried an antenna to talk directly to Earth and a TV camera that controllers moved remotely. It was used to broadcast the Apollo 15, 16 and 17 liftoffs from the Moon.
Los tres siguen aparcados cerca de los s: All three are still parked near the Hadley-Apennine, Descartes and Taurus-Littrow sites, where their crews left them.
Estaciones científicas automáticas en la: Automatic scientific stations on the surface
Apolo 12, 14, 15, 16 y 17 (el Apolo 11 l: Apollo 12, 14, 15, 16 and 17 (Apollo 11 carried a simpler version, the EASEP)
Sismómetros, magnetómetros, detectores d: Seismometers, magnetometers, particle detectors, heat-flow probes...
Hasta el 30 de septiembre de 1977, cuand: Until 30 September 1977, when NASA switched them off
Cada estación tenía una central que envi: Each station had a central unit that sent data to Earth and several experiments connected by cables. The seismometers detected moonquakes and meteorite impacts and helped reveal the Moon's interior.
Los retrorreflectores láser de los Apolo: The laser retroreflectors of Apollo 11, 14 and 15 need no power. Observatories still fire lasers at them today to measure the distance to the Moon to within centimetres: that's how we know it moves away about 3.8 cm a year.
Las estaciones están apagadas, pero los: The stations are switched off, but the retroreflectors still bounce back the light of lasers from Earth.
Unos 1000 kg al despegar y unos 300 kg a: About 1,000 kg at launch and about 300 kg on landing
Cámara de televisión; la Surveyor 3 llev: TV camera; Surveyor 3 carried a scoop to dig
Antes de enviar astronautas había que sa: Before sending astronauts, NASA had to know whether the lunar soil could hold a spacecraft or was a sea of dust to sink into. The Surveyors came down braking with rockets and proved a soft landing was possible.
En noviembre de 1969, el Apolo 12 aluniz: In November 1969, Apollo 12 landed about 180 m from Surveyor 3. The astronauts visited it and brought back its camera and other parts to study how space had changed them.
Las Surveyor siguen en la Luna; a la Sur: The Surveyors are still on the Moon; Surveyor 3 is missing the parts Apollo 12 took home.
4 jul 1997 · Ares Vallis, rebotando con: 4 Jul 1997 · Ares Vallis, bouncing on airbags
83 soles; su misión estaba planeada para: 83 sols; its mission was planned for 7
Mars Pathfinder probó una forma nueva y: Mars Pathfinder tested a new, low-cost way to reach Mars: fall wrapped in airbags and bounce until it stopped. Then little Sojourner rolled down a ramp and became the first rover on another planet.
Analizó rocas con su espectrómetro de ra: It analyzed rocks with its X-ray spectrometer and travelled about 100 m, always close to the lander, which served as its antenna to talk to Earth.
Cuando el módulo dejó de responder, en 1: When the lander stopped responding in 1997, Sojourner lost its link. It is still near the Carl Sagan Memorial Station, the name given to the lander.
Spirit: 4 ene 2004, cráter Gusev · Oppor: Spirit: 4 Jan 2004, Gusev crater · Opportunity: 25 Jan 2004, Meridiani Planum
Planeados para 90 soles. Spirit: hasta 2: Planned for 90 sols. Spirit: until 2010 · Opportunity: until 2018
Los rovers gemelos eran geólogos robótic: The twin rovers were robotic geologists: they had panoramic cameras, spectrometers and a tool to grind into rocks. Their job was to look for clues of water in Mars's past.
Opportunity encontró las «blueberries»,: Opportunity found the "blueberries", small hematite spheres that form in water. Spirit, with a jammed wheel, dragged it and uncovered soil that was almost pure silica, another sign of hot water.
Spirit quedó atascada en arena en 2009 y: Spirit got stuck in sand in 2009 and didn't survive the winter. Opportunity went silent in 2018 during a dust storm that covered the whole planet.
Spirit descansa en Troy, dentro del crát: Spirit rests at Troy, inside Gusev crater. Opportunity rests in Perseverance Valley, on the rim of Endeavour crater.
20 jul 1976, Chryse Planitia · 3 sep 197: 20 Jul 1976, Chryse Planitia · 3 Sep 1976, Utopia Planitia
Cada misión Viking tenía un orbitador y: Each Viking mission had an orbiter and a lander. The landers took the first photos from the surface of Mars and measured its weather for years.
También hicieron los primeros experiment: They also ran the first experiments to search for life on another planet: they scooped soil with an arm and analyzed it in small onboard labs. The results were ambiguous and are still debated.
Siguen en las llanuras de Chryse y Utopi: They are still on the Chryse and Utopia plains, thousands of kilometres apart, covered in dust.
Phoenix: 25 may 2008, cerca del polo nor: Phoenix: 25 May 2008, near the north pole · InSight: 26 Nov 2018, Elysium Planitia
Phoenix: hasta nov 2008 · InSight: hasta: Phoenix: until Nov 2008 · InSight: until Dec 2022
Hielo de agua bajo el suelo · más de 130: Water ice under the soil · more than 1,300 marsquakes
Phoenix excavó el suelo helado del Ártic: Phoenix dug into the frozen soil of the Martian Arctic with its robotic arm and confirmed there is water ice under the surface. When polar winter arrived it ran out of sunlight and never woke up again.
InSight colocó un sismómetro sobre el su: InSight placed a seismometer on the ground and recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes. Thanks to them we know what Mars's crust, mantle and core are like. Dust slowly covered its panels until it ran out of power.
Los dos siguen donde aterrizaron: Phoeni: Both remain where they landed: Phoenix on the icy northern plains and InSight in Elysium Planitia.
18 feb 2021 · bajo el rover Perseverance: 18 Feb 2021 · under the Perseverance rover, Jezero crater
Dos rotores de 1,2 m que giran en sentid: Two 1.2 m rotors spinning in opposite directions
19 abr 2021: primer vuelo propulsado y c: 19 Apr 2021: first powered, controlled flight on another planet
Ingenuity era una demostración tecnológi: Ingenuity was a technology demonstration: Mars's air is so thin that flying there is like flying more than 30 km high on Earth. Its blades had to spin very fast to hold it up.
Debía volar hasta 5 veces en 30 días, pe: It was meant to fly up to 5 times in 30 days, but it flew 72 times over almost three years and served as an aerial scout for Perseverance. In January 2024 its blades were damaged and it could no longer fly.
Se quedó en tierra en el cráter Jezero,: It stayed on the ground in Jezero crater, now a stationary artifact.
Pioneer 10: primera en visitar Júpiter (: Pioneer 10: first to visit Jupiter (1973) · Pioneer 11: first to visit Saturn (1979)
Últimas señales: Pioneer 11 en 1995 y Pi: Last signals: Pioneer 11 in 1995 and Pioneer 10 in 2003
Las Pioneer 10 y 11 abrieron el camino a: Pioneer 10 and 11 opened the way to the outer planets. They proved it was possible to cross the asteroid belt and survive Jupiter's radiation, and sent back the first close-up images of Jupiter and Saturn.
Las dos llevan una placa de aluminio dor: Both carry a gold-anodized aluminium plaque conceived by Carl Sagan and Frank Drake, with drawings by Linda Salzman Sagan: a man, a woman, the solar system and the Sun's position relative to 14 pulsars.
Viajan en silencio fuera del sistema sol: They drift silently out of the solar system. Pioneer 10 is heading toward the star Aldebaran: it would take more than 2 million years to get there.
Primera nave en orbitar dos cuerpos más: First spacecraft to orbit two bodies beyond Earth and the Moon, and the first to orbit a dwarf planet
1 nov 2018, sin combustible para orienta: 1 Nov 2018, out of fuel to point itself
Los motores iónicos empujan muy suave, p: Ion engines push very gently, but nonstop for years. Thanks to them, Dawn could enter orbit around Vesta, leave it and travel on to Ceres, something impossible with chemical rockets its size.
En Ceres descubrió manchas brillantes de: At Ceres it discovered bright salt deposits in Occator crater: the remains of salty water that rose from inside the dwarf planet.
Apagada, sigue en órbita alrededor de Ce: Switched off, it remains in orbit around Ceres, and is expected to stay there for decades.
NEAR (Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous) es: NEAR (Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous) studied the asteroid Eros, a rock about 34 km long, for a year and photographed it in great detail. It was named after Eugene Shoemaker, a pioneer in the study of impacts.
No estaba diseñada para aterrizar, pero: It wasn't designed to land, but at the end of the mission it descended slowly to the surface and kept sending data from there for days.
Sigue posada sobre Eros, un asteroide qu: It is still resting on Eros, an asteroid that orbits the Sun near Earth.
Kepler miraba siempre la misma zona del: Kepler stared at the same patch of sky and measured the brightness of about 150,000 stars at once. When a planet passed in front of its star, the brightness dipped a little: that's how it found thousands of worlds.
Cuando fallaron dos de sus ruedas de ori: When two of its reaction wheels failed, engineers used the pressure of sunlight to steady it and a second mission, K2, began. Kepler showed that our galaxy has more planets than stars.
Apagado, sigue a la Tierra en su órbita: Switched off, it trails Earth in its orbit around the Sun, drifting a little farther from us over time.
